'''Edward Lee House II''' (born May 14, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A [[guard (basketball)|guard]] known for his three-point shooting, House played for nine NBA teams in 11 seasons in the league. He was a member of the [[Boston Celtics]] team that won the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] championship in 2008, and is currently an analyst for Celtics games on [[NBC Sports Boston]].<ref name=":0" />

==Early life==
House was born in the city of [[Berkeley, California]], and was raised primarily in [[Union City, California]], where he attended [[James Logan High School]]. He transferred to [[Hayward High School (California)|Hayward High School]] because he was forbidden from playing on the Logan varsity team in his freshman year. At Hayward, he was named All-Hayward Area Athletic League and All-Eastbay in both his junior and senior years, and graduated in 1996. He wanted to play for [[University of California, Berkeley]], but coaches of that school felt that House was not ready for a major college basketball program, and recommended that House begin at a junior college.<ref name="Tri-city">{{cite web|last=Michel|first=Steve|title=An outside game|url=http://www.tricityvoice.com/articlefiledisplay.php?issue=2007-01-02&file=An+outsidegame.txt|work=Tri-City Voice|access-date=January 12, 2011|date=January 2, 2007|archive-date=July 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717101609/http://www.tricityvoice.com/articlefiledisplay.php?issue=2007-01-02&file=An+outsidegame.txt|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== College career ==
House attended [[Arizona State University]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]], on a full-ride scholarship.<ref name="Tri-city"/> He is the all-time scoring leader at ASU with 2,044 points in his career, and is the only player to score more than 2,000 points. He, [[Ike Diogu]], and [[James Harden]] are the only three [[Arizona State Sun Devils|Sun Devils]] to be named [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]], and he was the fifth Sun Devil to be voted onto the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Conference]] team twice.

He also is the career record-holder at Arizona State for [[Field goal (basketball)|field goals]] and [[Steal (basketball)|steals]], and set the single-season scoring average record for the school with 23.0 points per game in 1999–2000. During that season he was named Pac-10 ''Player of the Week'' a record-tying four times (matched only by [[Ed O'Bannon]], [[Chris Mills (basketball)|Chris Mills]], [[Gary Payton]], and [[Quincy Pondexter]]).

House set a single-game Arizona State record with a 61-point effort in a 111–108 double-overtime victory against the [[California Golden Bears]] on the road in his senior season. The point total tied the [[Pac-10]]'s single game record and was the highest total for the [[1999–2000 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/409393724|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|409393724}}|title=Points Well Made: [FINAL Edition]|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|accessdate=April 22, 2023|date=January 25, 2003|page=|author=|quote=}}</ref> It also was a memorable homecoming of sorts for him, as he had starred in high school for nearby Hayward High School. House also set a record in the game with 18 made free throws in 19 attempts. House is the first Pac-10 player to notch four 40-point games in one season as he had 61 vs. Cal, 46 vs. San Diego State, 42 vs. Penn State and 40 vs. UCLA. He also posted eight 30-point games that same season and set ASU records in points (736) and points per game (23.0). Also led the team in assists (111) and steals (74), as the 74 steals is tied for second on ASU single-season list. He is one of only three players to average in double figures in four consecutive seasons at Arizona State since it joined the Pac-10.

Prior to the [[2014 Fiesta Bowl (December)|2014 Fiesta Bowl]], House gave a motivational speech to the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos football team]] on the importance of beating their opponent, the [[Arizona Wildcats football|University of Arizona Wildcats]]. The Broncos won 38–30.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rosenblatt |first1=Zack |title=Seen and Heard in Scottsdale: Familiar Face |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/213719957/ |access-date=29 October 2024 |work=Arizona Daily Star |date=30 December 2014}}</ref>

== NBA career ==
In the NBA, House was known for his three-point shooting.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/2017/4/12/16041920/nba-game-82-all-stars-michael-beasley-jordan-mccrae-eddie-house-6c1f08dd3c4f|title = The Game 82 All-Stars|date = April 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/numbers-top-celtics-all-time-44-66|title=By the Numbers: Top C's of All Time – 44–66|website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

He was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] in the second round (37th overall) of the [[2000 NBA draft]]. He played in Miami for three seasons before leaving for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in free agency. After just one year in Los Angeles, House was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. He then spent the [[2004–05 NBA season]] playing for Charlotte, [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and [[Sacramento Kings]]. The following season House was signed by the [[Phoenix Suns]]; they reached the Western Conference Finals before losing to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].

On August 17, 2006, he signed a one-year, $1.5 million deal with the [[New Jersey Nets]].

[[File:Eddie House receives NBA championship ring.jpg|thumb|right|300px|House receiving his [[2008 NBA Finals]] ring]]
On August 9, 2007, he signed a one-year, $1.5 million deal with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>[http://www.bostonherald.com/blogs/sports/celtics/?p=121 Celts sign Eddie House], ''Boston Herald''</ref><ref>Chris Sheridan, [https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2957622 Boston starts to rebuild roster, signs House to one-year deal], ''ESPN.com''</ref> He joined a cast of all-stars dubbed as the Big Three – [[Paul Pierce]], [[Kevin Garnett]] and [[Ray Allen]]. The team won the [[2008 NBA Finals]] with House playing as a backup guard for either Ray Allen or [[Rajon Rondo]]. He played a pivotal role in the team's comeback victory in Game 4, knocking down two clutch three-pointers down the stretch.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.celticsblog.com/2013/9/5/4696224/most-hyped-the-2008-boston-celtics-bench-eddie-house-and-james-posey-nba-finals|title=Most Hyped-The '08 Bench-Eddie House & James Posey|date=September 5, 2013|website=CelticsBlog|access-date=May 9, 2017}}</ref> On July 23, 2008, he re-signed with the Celtics on a 2-year, $5.6 million deal, with the second year as player's option.<ref>Frank Dell'Apa, [http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2008/07/22/celtics_rebound_re_sign_allen_house/ Celtics rebound, re-sign Allen, House], ''[[Boston Globe]]'', July 22, 2008.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/transactions/jul2008_transactions.html |title=NBA.com: July 2008 Transactions |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 12, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090710010335/http://www.nba.com/transactions/jul2008_transactions.html |archive-date=July 10, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During the 2008–09 regular season, he broke [[Danny Ainge]]'s Celtics team record for best 3-point percentage in a season by shooting 44.4%.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/BOS/leaders_season.html Boston Celtics Season Leaders]</ref>

On February 18, 2010, House, [[Bill Walker (basketball)|Bill Walker]] and [[J.R. Giddens]] were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] for [[Nate Robinson]] and [[Marcus Landry]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Acquire Eddie House, J.R. Giddens and Bill Walker |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/celtics_trade1002.html |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date=February 19, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221041057/http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/celtics_trade1002.html |archive-date=February 21, 2010 }}</ref>

In July 2010 House's agent said that the guard agreed to terms on a $2.8 million, two-year contract to return to the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>[http://www.miamiherald.com/2010/07/29/1752129/miami-heat-signs-guard-eddie-house.html Eddie House rejoins Miami Heat with two-year deal], ''The Miami Herald''</ref>
[[File:Eddie House Heat.jpg|thumb|upright|House with the Miami Heat in 2010]]
On April 13, 2011, vs the [[Toronto Raptors]], House scored a career high 35 points, beating his career [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] record by four points. The Heat made the [[2011 NBA Finals]] and were defeated by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in six games. Game 6 of that Finals series ended up being House's final NBA game ever. The Heat lost Game 6 95–105 and House recorded 9 points, 3 rebounds, 1 assist and 1 steal.

On June 30, 2011, House exercised an option clause in his contract, agreeing to a one-year, $1.4 million extension with the Heat.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/news/story?id=6725264 Eddie House to remain with Heat]</ref> On Christmas Eve, he was waived by the Heat without playing a game for them during the 2011–2012 season.

== Personal life ==
[[File:Eddie and Jaelen House 030724.jpg|thumb|upright|Eddie (left) and Jaelen House in 2024]]
House is the son of Edward House and Deborah Buck, and he has two brothers, Diallo Buck and Mychal House. During his rookie season with [[Miami Heat|Miami]] in [[2000–01 NBA season|2000–01]], he married the sister of professional basketball player [[Mike Bibby]]. The couple has three sons: Jaelen, who played basketball for [[Arizona State University|Arizona State]] for one year before transferring to the [[University of New Mexico]]; and twins Kaden and Kalek. House and his wife later divorced. Both House and Bibby played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] in [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] and the [[Miami Heat]] in [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11]].

House is an analyst on [[NBC Sports Boston]]'s Celtics pre- and post-game shows, and is a fill-in color commentator for Celtics broadcasts on the network.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Finn |first=Chad |date=April 22, 2023 |title=Having Brian Scalabrine and Eddie House on Friday’s Celtics broadcast was a fine call |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2023/04/22/nbc-sports-boston-brian-scalabrine-eddie-house-announcers-celtics-hawks-game-3-4/ |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=www.boston.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
